relevance_note: National survey describing 54 HA20 patients individually in supplementary tables: "All 54 patients analyzed had heterozygous variants in TNFAIP3".
method_note: Rows built with a Python script in the scratch directory; per-patient values were transcribed by hand from my reading of Supplementary Tables 1 and 2 and the pedigree figure text, and every span was taken from or checked against the paper text by script. Labels: the paper's own P1-P54 (the form used in all supplementary tables); family labels F1-F37 from Supplementary Table 1. Scope: the 54 surveyed patients; relatives with individual-level facts (mother of P3 and father of P18, both with low-frequency somatic mosaicism and no printed variant; father of P38 and grandmother of P15, each with malignant lymphoma); two excluded people with somatic TNFAIP3 mosaicism (unnamed person 1, c.806-1G>T, 22%; unnamed person 2, p.Q760X, 14%) and the two symptomatic family members of unnamed person 2 who did not carry the variant. Not given rows: the 20 excluded missense cases (Supplementary Table 6 lists 16 variants with no per-person detail), the three asymptomatic heterozygous carriers mentioned only as a count, and pedigree-only individuals. Variants: Supplementary Table 1 gives mostly protein-only genotypes; cDNA strings come from the pedigree figure (Image1.pdf), where each family header line ('FamilyN') is followed by 'DNA alteration:' and 'AA alteration:' lines in the same left-to-right order. I matched them by family number and column order; every protein string in the figure agreed with Supplementary Table 1 for the same family, which supports the mapping, but it is a reading of a converted figure layout. Variant values with markdown escapes (c.806-1G\>T) are recorded without the backslash; spans keep it. Zygosity 'heterozygous' and pathogenicity 'pathogenic' for P1-P54 come from the named-group statement 'All 54 patients analyzed had heterozygous variants in TNFAIP3, comprising a total of 35 distinct pathogenic variants.' Variant type is filled only where the paper names the variant with its class: missense for p.E192K and p.C243Y; splice for c.487-1G>A, c.805+1G>A and c.2088+1G>A (minigene section); large deletion/CNV for the deletion genotypes. Functional evidence is the minigene result for the named splice variant, and the exon 8 skipping statement for P3. Inheritance is not reported for everyone (no statement that a named parent carries the same variant). Phenotypes: Supplementary Table 2 uses '+', '-' and '−'; no legend defines '-' or '−' as absent, so those cells are 'not reported' and no checklist item is excluded from them. 'Intestinal symptoms +' is recorded as a feature but not as 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' (symptoms are not ulcers or inflammation). 'Ulcer (oral/genital)' cells such as '+/−' are read as oral then genital. Cells with abbreviations are expanded with the legend (AD, EN, AIH, AIHA, ITP, SLE, SS, HLH), quoting the legend as a second span. Suspected findings were not recorded as observed (P11 'PFAPA (suspected)', P53 'AIH susp'). Initial-diagnosis column values were not turned into features. IFN score 'Normal' (P13, P20, P21) is recorded as excluded 'elevated IFN score' (D-27); 'Elevated' as observed. Ethnicity: 'Japanese' for all but P51 from 'Fifty-three of the patients were Japanese and one was Vietnamese (patient 51).' Malignant lymphoma onset ages (21, 35, 70) for P8, father of P38 and grandmother of P15 come from the paper's own 'respectively' list. No stacked multi-patient cells were read by position (Supplementary Table 2 has one patient per row; ' / ' there separates lines inside one patient's cell). Contradictions and oddities: (1) the legend of Supplementary Table 2 defines 'HS, Hashimoto’s disease' but the table uses 'HD'; I read HD as Hashimoto’s disease (8 HD cells match 'Hashimoto’s disease (8)' in Table 2) and marked autoimmune thyroiditis observed for P5, P6, P7, P8, P9, P27, P36, P53; (2) P49's variant is c.2088+1G>A in Supplementary Table 1 and the pedigree but 'c.2099 + 1G>A' in the Results text; the table value is used; (3) the minigene methods list c.986+1G>T while all results and Supplementary Table 1 (P50) give c.986+1G>C, so P50's variant type is left not reported; (4) Family 19's pedigree protein is p.Asn212GlufsX while the minigene result gives p.Asp212GlufsX; (5) Family 13's cDNA is printed 'c.1434C<A'; recorded as printed; (6) Table 2 counts acute encephalopathy (3) and the Discussion mentions three patients with encephalopathy, but only P38 is named with it in the text and Supplementary Table 2; (7) Supplementary Table 2 has 20 patients with a genital ulcer '+' while Table 2 counts 19; each row was recorded as printed; (8) the CNS checklist item is observed only for the five patients the text names (P10, P33, P38, P44, P47); headache, ataxia and psychiatric symptoms in other patients are recorded as features only.
